committedOct 11, 2026
Give the Greek words Abbott-Smith's and Thayer's entries, and their roots
Abbott-Smith's Manual Greek Lexicon (1922, public domain, the TEI of the Translatable Exegetical Tools project) and Thayer's Greek-English Lexicon (1889, public domain, a CC0 machine reading) are prepared with STEP Bible's files. Each entry finds the TR's dictionary forms it describes by the Strong's numbers TAGNT and it share, failing those its spelling, and is written out keyed by those forms alone: no Strong's number leaves the prepare step. A Thayer entry split over a page is joined, and his references (Lk. iv. 17, 20) become links. Each form is given the roots it is built on, found by following the lexicons' derivations back: Abbott-Smith's (< λέγω), Thayer's (fr. ἀγαθοποιός), a compound's hyphenated last element (ἐκ-βάλλω). A compound of two words has both roots; a prefixed preposition, privative or adverb is none. 5,409 of the TR's 5,419 forms have an entry, built on 2,698 roots. gen-runtime and gen-greek write greek_dictionary, greek_dictionary_form and greek_root, the entries compressed against a dictionary of their own where the database compresses its blobs. Bible::greek_roots, greek_lexicon_entries, greek_lexicon_entry, greek_root_lemmas and greek_root_occurrences read them. The lexicons, and Jastrow, write "Yahweh" where they had "Jehovah", except where Klein speaks of the transliteration itself. The READMEs credit TAGNT, Abbott-Smith and Thayer. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
